images.title: An even count closes, an odd count opens
images.purpose: Before and after comparison: locker 12 is toggled 6 times and ends closed, locker 16 is toggled 5 times and ends open.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two tall lockers side by side with wide space between them, each with a row of tally marks under it.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 2 tall locker doors of equal size, side by side. Left locker numbered 12 on a plate near its top, drawn closed and filled teal (#0072B2); under it exactly 6 short vertical tally marks in a row, labelled 6 toggles, and under that the word closed. Right locker numbered 16, drawn with its door swung open to show a white inside, door filled reddish purple (#CC79A7); under it exactly 5 short vertical tally marks in a row, labelled 5 toggles, and under that the word open. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A locker ends open only when its number has an odd number of factors, that is, when it is a square.
images.description: Before and after comparison: locker 12 is toggled 6 times and ends closed, locker 16 is toggled 5 times and ends open.

image_decisions.why: Comparing one non square and one square locker side by side shows the whole rule for solving the puzzle.
